title: Air Filter Devices Including Nonwoven Meshes of Electrospun Recombinant Spider Silk Proteins
protocol: Take lyophilized eADF4(C16) protein.
Weigh 20 mg of eADF4(C16).
Add 200 μl of hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP).
Seal the vessel with Parafilm.
Vortex the suspension for 1 min.
Shake the suspension to clear the solution.
Wait overnight to ensure complete dissolution.
Place filter material on top of the counter electrode.
Preset the voltage of both electrodes: -22.5 kV and +2.5 kV.
Set the volume flow to 315 μl/hr.
Grind the tip of a 20 G needle with a hand grinder to a residual length of 30 mm.
Connect the modified needle to a 1 ml syringe.
Load the entire spinning dope (200 μl) into the syringe.
Overlay the dope in the syringe with 100 μl of air.
Work under a fume hood.
Mix the solution to ensure there are no particles in it.
Attach the filled syringe to the syringe pump of the electrospinning device.
Press the piston onto the syringe until a droplet appears at the tip of the needle.
Lock the piston.
Set the distance between the tip of the needle and the counter electrode to 8-20 cm.
Start the syringe pump.
Remove the dried out droplet from the opening of the needle immediately.
Activate all safety installations of the electrospinning device.
Start the high voltage source as soon as a new droplet appears at the needle tip.
Use a stopwatch to control spinning duration.
Pre-heat an oven to 60 °C.
Place filter substrates with eADF4(C16) nonwoven meshes vertically and with a minimum distance of 2 cm in a lockable glass container.
Stop the electrospinning process after 5 min.
Connect two 60 ml syringes, one filled with ethanol and one filled with water, with silicone tubes pointing into the interior bottom of the post-treatment container.
Place the post-treatment container in the oven and add 60 ml of ethanol by extruding the syringe.
Use a stopwatch to control treatment duration for 90 min.
Remove the ethanol with the syringe from the glass after 90 min.
Add 60 ml of water from the second syringe into the post-treatment container.
Wait for another 90 min.
Remove the water and switch off the oven.
Leave the container in the oven until it has completely cooled down to avoid droplets by condensation.
Prepare the silk nonwoven meshes for stability tests on black paper or any other removable support.
Cut two frames out of cardboard and adjust double-sticky adhesive tape.
Press one frame onto the silk nonwoven mesh deposited on black paper and use a scalpel to cut off the excess of silk fibers.
Carefully remove the frame in order to detach the nonwoven from the paper.
Repeat this step with the second frame.
Cut a piece (1 cm²) of each post-treated and non-treated silk nonwoven mesh.
Dip the cut pieces into deionized water.
Dry the dipped samples after removal from water.
Prepare the dried samples for SEM imaging.
Measure FTIR spectra in transmittance mode from 800 to 4,000 cm⁻¹ with 60 accumulations per spectrum.
Perform Fourier self-deconvolution (FSD) on the measured FTIR data between 1,590 and 1,705 cm⁻¹.
Apply baseline correction and local least square fit for quantitative analysis based on peak positions from previous studies.
Conduct SEM imaging to investigate fiber diameters and morphology of silk fibers under magnifications ranging from 5,000x to 25,000x.
Place a proper fitting part of the filter material on the measuring area of an Akustron air permeability device.
Repeat steps 1 and 2 at least 10 times with different parts of your sample.
Calculate the arithmetic mean of the normed data [l / (m² x sec)].
Use a machine with pressure control and particle counter, such as a Universal particle sizer.
Place the filter samples in the device.

Measure particle retention using Di-ethyl-hexyl-sebacat (DEHS) aerosol with particle sizes ranging from 0.3 to 3 μm for 30 seconds at a liquid velocity of 2,350 cm/sec and an air flow rate of 3,400 m³/hr.
Handle the sample with care to prevent destruction of the nonwoven mesh and avoid pollution.
